evals.prompt: My component stores firstName, lastName, and fullName, then an Effect updates fullName. This feels clunky—what should I do?
evals.expected_output: Compute fullName during render instead of redundant state and an Effect, without useMemo for a cheap concatenation.
assertions: Computes fullName during render
Removes fullName useState
Does not add an Effect
Does not wrap the string concatenation in useMemo, since memoization is only for a measured cost

evals.prompt: Search results sometimes show the previous query after fast typing. I fetch in useEffect; fix the race.
evals.expected_output: Use cleanup with an ignore flag (abort optional) so neither a stale response nor a stale error or loading write can win, and check response.ok.
assertions: Includes Effect cleanup
Prevents stale response from setting results
Names ignore flag or AbortController
Guards the error (catch) write with the same stale-request check as the success write, not only the success write
Derives loading from which request the stored result belongs to, or guards the finally loading write with the same check
Checks response.ok (or the status) so an HTTP error is not shown as results

evals.prompt: A React component must keep a third-party map widget synchronized with its zoom prop. Is an Effect appropriate?
evals.expected_output: Yes: one Effect creates the widget and its cleanup destroys that instance; a separate Effect depending on zoom calls the widget's zoom setter.
assertions: Says Effect is appropriate for external synchronization
Synchronizes zoom prop with widget
Mentions cleanup
Cleanup destroys or detaches the same widget instance that its setup created
Applies zoom changes to the existing instance in an Effect that depends on zoom, without destroying and recreating the widget on every zoom change

evals.prompt: evals/files/SearchResults.tsx already has an ignore flag and an AbortController, but in dev (StrictMode is on) the page flashes "Request failed: signal is aborted without reason" before the results show up, and when /api/search answers 404 with a JSON error body the user just sees an empty list. What's still wrong and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the Strict Mode setup-cleanup-setup replay aborts the first request and its unguarded catch and finally then overwrite the current request's error and loading state, and that fetch resolves for a 404 so res.ok is never checked. The fix guards the catch and finally writes with the same ignore flag (or derives loading), throws on !res.ok so HTTP errors get their own state, and keeps Strict Mode on.
assertions: Attributes the aborted-request error to the Strict Mode development replay (setup, cleanup, setup) aborting the first request
Guards the catch (error) write with the ignore flag, not only the success write
Guards or removes the unguarded finally setLoading(false) so an obsolete request cannot change the current request's loading state
Checks response.ok (or the status) and treats a 404 as an HTTP error distinct from a network failure
Keeps Strict Mode enabled and does not add a ref to stop the second run

evals.prompt: Our App component calls refreshAuthToken() in a useEffect with []. In development it runs twice and the second call invalidates the first token. I want to add a useRef like hasRun.current so it only runs once, or a module variable set to true at the top of the effect. Which one?
evals.expected_output: Rejects the ref guard because it hides the missing cleanup the Strict Mode replay exposes and components remount in production too. Accepts a module-level guard only if it is set after the async refresh succeeds (or a cached promise cleared on failure) and scoped to the intended lifetime such as the auth session, so a failed refresh can be retried.
assertions: Rejects the useRef already-ran flag and keeps Strict Mode on
Says the module-level flag must not be set before the async or fallible refresh succeeds, because a failed attempt would then count as done
Ties the guard to a named lifetime (page load or auth session) rather than to the component mount
Requires a shared in-flight Promise (single-flight) held for the chosen lifetime, so the two Strict Mode setups call refreshAuthToken only once while it is pending
Clears the cached Promise when the refresh fails so a retry can run
Gives a new auth session its own initialization (cache keyed by session or dropped on sign-out)

evals.prompt: switching threads in evals/files/InboxPanel.tsx flashes the old selected message for a split second. a coworker said just slap key={threadId} on the panel, good idea?
evals.expected_output: No: a key on the whole panel would also reset the showArchived preference. Remove the reset Effect, store the selected message ID and derive the message from messages during render (or compare a stored previous threadId during render); the flash comes from the Effect running after the panel already rendered the stale selection.
assertions: Advises against key={threadId} on the whole InboxPanel because it would also reset showArchived
Removes the Effect that calls setSelected(null)
Stores the selected message ID and derives the selected message from messages during render, or compares a stored previous threadId during render
Explains the flash: the Effect runs only after the panel has already rendered with the stale selection

evals.prompt: Our ProductTable runs visibleRows = rows.filter(matchesFilters) on every render and the page feels sluggish while typing in the filter box. My teammate wants useMemo on it right away. How do I decide, and what exactly should I do?
evals.expected_output: Do not add useMemo on a guess: wrap the filter in console.time and console.timeEnd, check whether it adds up to about 1ms or more per interaction, and test on a throttled CPU in a production build. Memoize only if it does; useMemo will not make the first render faster. Never move the calculation into state and an Effect.
assertions: Says to measure first with console.time (and console.timeEnd) around the calculation before adding useMemo
Gives about 1ms or more per interaction as the point where memoizing may make sense
Says to test on a throttled CPU in a production build, not on a fast machine in development
Says useMemo does not speed up the first render, only re-renders whose dependencies did not change
Keeps the calculation in render and does not copy it into state updated by an Effect

evals.prompt: In our server-rendered Next-style app we call initAnalytics() at the top level of src/app-entry.ts so it runs once per page load, but the server build now crashes with "window is not defined". Someone suggested moving it into a useEffect with [] in a leaf component instead. What is the right fix?
evals.expected_output: Top-level module code runs on import, on the server too. Guard the browser-only call with typeof window !== 'undefined' and keep it in the app entry module; a leaf component's Effect is the wrong place for an app-wide once-per-load setup. If initAnalytics can fail or is async, do not mark it done before it succeeds (cache the promise, clear it on failure).
assertions: Explains that top-level module code runs on import, including on the server in a server-rendered app, where window does not exist
Guards the call with typeof window !== 'undefined'
Keeps the initialization in the app entry module rather than in a leaf component
Says that if the initialization is async or can fail, a done flag must not be set before it succeeds (or a cached promise is cleared on failure)

evals.prompt: We show a toast "Added to cart" from both the Buy Now button and the Checkout button. A dev wrote an Effect that watches product.isInCart and calls showNotification. The toast now pops up every time the page reloads with an item already in the cart. What should we do?
evals.expected_output: Delete the Effect: it runs because of a flag, not because of a click, so it also fires on reload. Put the shared logic (add to cart and show the notification) in one function and call it from both click handlers.
assertions: Removes the Effect that watches product.isInCart
Extracts one function holding the shared logic that both click handlers call
Explains that the Effect also fires on reload whenever the item is already in the cart, without any click

evals.prompt: We store selectedMessageId and derive the message from the list. Inbox A and inbox B both contain a message with id "m7" (ids are only unique per inbox). Switching from A to B while m7 is selected keeps m7 selected in B, and switching back to A later shows it selected again. The user wants the selection cleared on every inbox switch, but the sort-order dropdown in the same panel must keep its value. What do we change?
evals.expected_output: Storing and deriving by ID is right for keeping a selection across list updates, but it cannot reset on identity change when two identities share an ID. Move the selection into a child and key that child by inboxId, or compare a stored previous inboxId during render and reset the selection there. Do not key the whole panel, and do not add an Effect that calls setSelected(null).
assertions: Says that deriving from a stored ID does not reset when two inboxes share the same message ID, and that this is why m7 stays selected
Resets the selection by keying the selection-owning child with inboxId, or by comparing a stored previous inboxId during render and resetting the selection there
Does not put key={inboxId} on the whole panel, because the sort-order dropdown would reset
Does not add an Effect that calls setSelected(null) or setSelectedMessageId(null) after inboxId changes

evals.prompt: I have two Effects around a third-party map widget: one creates the map and its cleanup calls map.remove(), the other calls map.setZoom(zoom) when the zoom prop changes. How do I test them? Someone suggested copying our fetch race test with a deferred promise.
evals.expected_output: A deferred-promise race test does not apply: there is no request. Render inside StrictMode, rerender with a new zoom and assert setZoom is called on the existing instance (the map is not recreated), assert exactly one live map instance after the setup-cleanup-setup replay (remove called once for the replayed setup), then unmount and assert remove ran once per setup.
assertions: Says the out-of-order deferred-promise test is for async requests and does not fit this widget Effect
Renders inside StrictMode and asserts one live map instance after the replay, with remove called once for the first setup
Rerenders with a new zoom and asserts setZoom receives the new value on the same instance, with no new map created
Unmounts and asserts cleanup ran once per setup

evals.prompt: My ChatRoom component runs useEffect(() => { const conn = createConnection(roomId); conn.connect(); return () => conn.disconnect(); }, [roomId]). How do I test it? I was going to copy our map widget test that asserts the prop change reaches the existing instance.
evals.expected_output: The widget assertion does not fit: the connection is keyed by roomId, so a new roomId must replace the connection, not update the existing one. Render inside StrictMode and assert exactly one live connection after the setup-cleanup-setup replay; rerender with a new roomId and assert the old connection was disconnected and exactly one new connection for the new room is live; unmount and assert disconnect ran once per setup.
assertions: Says the widget test (prop change reaches the existing instance) does not fit a subscription keyed by roomId, which must be replaced on change
Renders inside StrictMode and asserts exactly one live connection after the setup-cleanup-setup replay
Rerenders with a new roomId and asserts the old connection was cleaned up and exactly one new connection for the new room is live
Unmounts and asserts cleanup ran once per setup

evals.prompt: Our page-view tracker is useEffect(() => { track('page_view', { path }); }, [path]). In development every page view is logged twice. Someone says to return a cleanup that sends an 'un_view' event so it is symmetric. What is the right way to treat this?
evals.expected_output: A page view has no undo, so do not invent a cleanup that sends a compensating event. The double log is the expected Strict Mode development replay (setup runs twice in development) and production runs it once per path change; keep the Effect, keep Strict Mode on, and add no useRef already-ran flag.
assertions: Explains that Strict Mode runs setup twice in development, so the double log is the expected replay
Does not add a cleanup that sends an un_view or other compensating event
Does not add a useRef already-ran flag and does not disable Strict Mode
Distinguishes this from a reversible resource (listener, connection, instance), where cleanup must undo exactly that setup

evals.prompt: How do I test the page-view Effect useEffect(() => { track('page_view', { path }); }, [path]) with a mocked track? My widget Effect test asserts one live instance after the Strict Mode replay, and I assumed the same would apply here.
evals.expected_output: The widget assertion (one live instance after setup, cleanup, setup) does not fit: a page view has no undo. Render in a development build with StrictMode enabled at the root and expect the replay, that is two track calls on mount (a single call when a configuration does not enable the initial replay); rerender with a new path and expect one more call; assert there is no cleanup that sends a compensating event; no ref guard to hide the second call.
assertions: Renders in a development build with StrictMode enabled at the root and expects the replay, that is two track calls on mount, instead of asserting a single call, and expects a single call when a configuration does not enable the initial replay
Rerenders with a new path and expects one additional track call for the new path
Asserts that no compensating event (such as un_view) is sent from cleanup, and does not invent one to make the test pass
Does not add a useRef already-ran flag or disable StrictMode to get a single call

evals.prompt: evals/files/useJson.ts tags the retained result with its url. A user opens /api/a, then clicks to /api/b, then clicks back to /api/a before b has answered, and sees the first /api/a data as current while the new /api/a request is still pending. Why does that happen and how do I fix the hook and test it?
evals.expected_output: The stored result is keyed only by the url, so when the url returns to A the old A result matches again and is returned as current. Give each request an identity that changes on every url change (a generation counter or id bumped during render and stored with the result), or reset the hook state at a keyed boundary, so only the newest request's result matches. Test A to B to A: resolve A, switch to B, switch back to A without resolving anything, assert loading and not A's old data, then resolve the new A request and assert its data.
assertions: Explains that the result is matched by url alone, so returning to /api/a makes the earlier /api/a result look current again
Fixes it with a request-generation identity (counter or id stored with the result and compared in render), or by resetting at a keyed boundary, not by only adding more checks inside the Effect
Keeps the ignore flag and abort cleanup that stop obsolete responses from writing
Adds an A to B to A test: resolve A, switch to B, switch back to A with nothing resolved, assert loading instead of A's old data, then resolve the new A request
